near_miss.lead: ON hvíla sér nótt / sofa um nóttina ~ Gk ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον (night + resting/sleeping)
near_miss.why_not: Shared roots are only *nókʷts (ON nótt ~ Gk νύξ); ON verb hvíla and Gk ἰαύω (*h2wes-) are not cognate, and the Homeric phrase is about sleepless nights (ἀ-ϋπνος), the ON about lying with a woman for one night. 'Night' + 'sleep' is universal language. Irish suan codladh (G301026) is an internal Irish doublet.

near_miss.lead: ON vann morg stor verk ~ Arm. mec en gorckʻ ~ Gk ἔργον ... μέγα ('great works', *wérǵom + big)
near_miss.why_not: Adjectives are not cognate (ON stórr/mikill, Arm. mec and Gk μέγας share *méǵh2- only with mikill, which is not the adjective on verk here); the Armenian is a quotation of Psalm 104:24 translated from Greek/Hebrew; 'great deeds' is generic.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 678 - PDF page 158 (word id 25631) (w1/2)
near_miss.lead: ON setja son í kné sér (knee-setting)
near_miss.why_not: No slab partner has the knee motif; Sanskrit and Armenian partners share only common roots. Tested in the corpora; see search lead.

near_miss.lead: ON (hefir firir gort) fé ok friði ~ Ved. paśūnām ... priyaṃ dhāma (*péḱu + *priH-)
near_miss.why_not: Different structures and senses: ON is a legal alliterative pair 'property and peace' (forfeits goods and protection), friðr = 'peace'; Ved. priyá 'dear' is an adjective on dhāman with paśūnām a genitive in a Vrātya refrain. Two very common roots, no shared collocation.

near_miss.lead: Kin-term coordination: ON dóttir ok systir / bróðir ~ Ved. duhitā ... svasā / bhrātrā svasrā ~ ORus. сестра и дъчи
near_miss.why_not: The cognate kin terms are inherited words, but listing daughter/sister/brother is enumerative (ON inheritance and wergild law lists, AV genealogical identification of a plant/disease, birchbark letter): no shared figure or syntax beyond coordination, which any kinship text produces.

near_miss.lead: ON sverða songr (battle kenning) ~ Gk θεοῦ ὀμφῇ (*sengʷʰ-)
near_miss.why_not: Only one shared root; ON kenning 'song of swords' = battle, Gk ὀμφή = divine utterance/oracle following the people; contexts unrelated.

near_miss.lead: ON snjór kemr ok fellr ~ Umbr. ninctu (snow) next to holtu
near_miss.why_not: ON is a legal date clause (when snow comes and falls), Umbrian an imprecation list of weather-calamities; ON falla and Umbr. holtu are not securely cognate and the Umbrian is not a fall-of-snow phrase.

near_miss.lead: ON bera orð föður síns ~ Lat. pater ... uerba det (*werdʰo- + father)
near_miss.why_not: ON 'bear (witness to) the father's word' in an odal-proof clause; Latin uerba dare is the idiom 'to cheat'; different verbs and senses.

near_miss.lead: ON ausa sveininn vatni (name-sprinkling) ~ Gk ἀφυσσάμενοι ... ὕδωρ ~ Lat. haustus (*h2ews- 'draw water' + water)
near_miss.why_not: ON ausa vatni here is the pagan naming rite; the Greek is fetching water for ships, and ἀφύσσω is not securely from *h2ews- (the Latin haurio/ON ausa equation is sound but 'draw water' + 'water' is the verb's basic use). The Irish partners (Finn's thumb under his tooth of knowledge) share only 'tooth' with the ON tannfé.

near_miss.lead: Exposure of a newborn: ON bera út barnit ~ Eur. Ion βρέφος νεογνόν
near_miss.why_not: Shared narrative motif (exposed royal child), but no cognate wording: ON barn/bera vs Gk βρέφος (not cognate), μήτηρ ~ móðir not in the ON clause.

near_miss.lead: ON verja oddi ok eggju ('defend with point and edge')
near_miss.why_not: A Germanic alliterative pair (cf. OE ord ond ecg, Gmc-internal); the AV partner (love charm with garment) has nothing comparable; no cross-branch partner known to me.

search_lead.cognate: ON kné ~ Gk γόνυ (dat. pl. γούνασι) ~ Hitt. genu- < *ǵónu; verb renewed (ON setja < *sodéye- vs Gk τίθημι < *dʰeh1-)
search_lead.argument: Placing a newborn on the knees of a (grand)father as the prelude to naming/acknowledgment: Od. 19.401ff Eurykleia sets the infant Odysseus on Autolykos' knees and asks him to give the name; ON knésetja is the rite of acknowledgment/fosterage and occurs with name-giving (AM-35-fol 115). Hittite Ullikummi (and Appu) have the child placed on the father's knees and then named (recalled; not found in the indexed Hittite). The slab anchor is a weak witness: Asta sets her son Olaf on her own knee to question him, not to name him; the rite context is better in the other ON loci.

error.evidence: List of women for whom a man may kill: kona manz, moðr manz, dotter, systir, stiupmoðr; 'moðr manz' is 'a man's mother', not móðr 'wrath/weariness'.

error.correct_reading: ræfr 'roof' belongs with Gk ἐρέφω/ὄροφος 'roof' (*h1rebʰ- 'to cover'), not with Lat. rapio
error.evidence: forn skemma ok af ræfrit = an old outhouse with the roof off; sense 'roof' is clear.
